title: The Void Throne v0.2 — three six-role simulations
method: Fresh five player roles plus one facilitator per run; isolated briefs, selected visions only, phase-scoped message packets. Role agents scheduled in batches within concurrency limits. Nominal game clock, not measured human play time. No rules changes between runs.

findings.lead: Two groups ratified a settlement; one did not. Named assets made their bargains specific, and cooperation carried real costs, unevenly shared. All three groups failed to enact provisional articles, leaving the intended trial of new constitutional powers untested.

compromises.guild: Actually missed the second contract to supply Relief. Ratified a continuing Lantern upkeep duty under N-G.
compromises.janissariat: Accepted one quiet month: Readiness 3→2, later restored to 3 by Raid. Ratified joint military authority and continuing Spear service; did not secure autonomy.
compromises.ascendant: Ratified loss of sole authority over both councils and loss of Warrant power under N-G/M-J. Kept Grey Petrel.
compromises.communities: Successful Raid imposed −2, alongside consumption and relief. Ended at 2, down from 3. This civilian loss is additional to player concessions.

compromises.guild: Completed both contracts; committed Lantern to upkeep and Repair. Refused the final compulsory Wayfarer service package, so that proposed duty never applied.
compromises.janissariat: Accepted a quiet second month: Readiness 4→3. Offered joint military scrutiny in the final package; it was not ratified.
compromises.ascendant: Actually spent Grey Petrel. Offered sole military command as a final concession while retaining Navigation; the offer failed, so no new constitutional powers were lost.
compromises.communities: Successful first-month Raid imposed −2. Relief, protection and distribution offset the harm; final Communities 4 does not mean the Raid was costless.

compromises.guild: Kept both contracts and all assets; ratified its preferred N-G/M-J package. New upkeep duty restricts future use of Lantern, but caused no missed contract in these two rounds.
compromises.janissariat: Withheld Spear and accepted Readiness 4→3. Ratified continuing Spear service and a shared military voice; gave up the autonomy and Navigation veto initially sought.
compromises.ascendant: Actually spent Grey Petrel, then ratified loss of both independent council powers and the Warrant. This was the largest transfer of existing power.
compromises.communities: First Raid imposed −2 over the humanitarian commander's objection. Relief and protection offset it; second-month Guard and distribution raised the final track to 4.

sections: The assets make the negotiation easier to specify

Players could point to Wayfarer, Lantern, Spear, Vigil and Grey Petrel when explaining a promise or refusal. Wayfarer could trade or carry council cargo; Lantern could maintain the beacon or support its single council action; Vigil could serve a Warrant or Guard, never both. Two vessels crossing meant two separate wear costs. Agents identified these relationships in their own reasoning and debriefs. This is useful evidence of clarity within the transcripts, not a measured comparison of human comprehension against the earlier token system.
Compromise is real, but the burdens are uneven

Run one obtained a settlement with a missed Guild contract, military scrutiny and substantial imperial delegation. Run two preserved both contracts but failed ratification. Run three kept both contracts and ratified the Guild's preferred package: the Guild's concession was a continuing upkeep duty, while the crown spent its reserve and lost both independent powers. The goal of making nearly everyone give something up is met more clearly through legal obligations than immediate material losses; these runs do not establish balanced sacrifice. A promise on an unsuccessful Charter is not a cost paid, and civilian suffering is not a sacrifice by the player ordering the Raid.
A quiet final month can be a small sacrifice

Readiness falling from 4 to 3 is a real counter loss, but both values have the same strong-support ending and meet the Readiness requirement for a Warrant where the Charter permits one. All five run-three players described that reduction as cheap in debrief. Early combat therefore buys an inexpensive quiet month at the end of this two-round scenario. By contrast, falling from 3 to 2 in run one removed a live imperial option. Do not count those two reductions as equally costly, or treat giving up a hoped-for autonomy article as losing a power the army already possessed.
The army's condition changes what the Ascendant can do

Runs one and two both ended at Readiness 3, but reached it differently. A peaceful opening in run one reduced Readiness to 2 and removed the next month's Warrant option. Early fighting in run two raised Readiness to 4, preserving that option in round two. The mechanism therefore gave the Ascendant a concrete reason to want a fighting army even while bargaining over a better government. In run three, the humanitarian commander explicitly accepted decline and opposed speculative violence; the Ascendant used offered Spear anyway under Interim authority. Operational coordination should not be described as unanimous political cooperation.
Foresight and unilateral choices had different levels of exposure

The Security visions were useful when they connected a live Raid choice to an actual voyage: run one coordinated Relief and Raid, and run two chose a productive first Raid then avoided an empty second one. Run three's second vision confirmed a repair plan after Spear had already been withheld. No Ascendant selected the second Navigation vision; its Repair/Trade benefit still applied in runs two and three. Private Trade was exercised repeatedly, and run three demonstrated imperial use of offered Spear over a delegate's objection, followed by the faction physically withholding it. No faction chose independent Raid; no Shared passage, Military/Campaign operation, permanent asset loss or triggered Tender cover occurred. Those branches remain behaviourally untested.
The constitutional experiment did not happen

No round-one council obtained matching article signatures in any of the three runs. Every round-two operation therefore used Interim authority. Players changed offers after seeing resource costs and the existing command arrangement, but none experienced a newly delegated power in operation. This is the clearest gap in the evidence. The bounded agent exchanges may have contributed: run one included late-delivered offers, and run three did not relay every addressed closing reply back before resolution. The games were not played against a human five- or seven-minute clock. Differences between runs cannot be attributed to personality alone, and this does not establish that live councils would fail to agree.
What the next paper test should check

Keep the named cards and use a brief spoken readback at each bell: asset, assignment, authorised use, and reserve trigger. Put the exact proposed Charter option and its three signatures in the centre of each council. Observe whether people can reach a provisional agreement with live conversation; if they repeatedly cannot, test moving that agreement deadline to the end of round-one free discussion in a later draft. Also allow a short faction discussion before the final replacement package. None of those changes was introduced during these v0.2 simulations.

GN.name: Mara
GN.temperament: Practical commercial negotiator. Medium willingness to compromise, low aggression. Named ships and missed contracts matter. Will trade discretion for a measurable return, but dislikes vague promises.

GS.name: Ivo
GS.temperament: Protective consensus builder. High willingness to compromise, low aggression. Navigator safety and civilian welfare dominate. Wants to find an agreement both Guild teammates can own; will challenge an unsafe plan.

JN.name: Cass
JN.temperament: Patient institutional reformer. High willingness to compromise, low-to-medium aggression. Values soldiers having a future, but takes Readiness decline seriously. Can accept civilian oversight for a workable military plan.

JS.name: Rhea
JS.temperament: Professional commander. Medium willingness to compromise, medium aggression. Prefers a properly supported campaign to gambling on a raid. Will accept restraint for one round if its institutional cost is acknowledged.

A.name: The Steward
A.temperament: Conciliatory long-term ruler. High willingness to compromise, medium risk tolerance. Will delegate a real power for stable institutions, but wants a usable army. Shares evidence when it can make an agreement possible.

messages.text: The two rounds represent two months before the Ceremony. Starting state: Beacon 2, Communities 3, Readiness 3; all four faction assets ready; Grey Petrel available; commercial contracts 0. Both domains are Interim: the Ascendant chooses both council orders. Asset assignments lock at each faction bell and cannot be reassigned during councils. Only offered assets can fund council orders. Round-one provisional articles require the separate signatures of both council delegates and the Ascendant and take effect in round two. Final settlement requires all five player approvals.

contributions.reason: Neutral rules briefing and opening public record.

Independent maintenance and trade protect our named assets, upkeep and first contract; reserve relief and Guard are requests requiring other parties, not assumed commitments. N-G protects navigation discretion and commercial freedom, while M-J gives our Security delegate a voice over violence.

messages.text: I propose Wayfarer Trade and Lantern Maintain: that prepares Beacon 3 and lets us meet our first contract without leaving Wayfarer dependent on Guard. Ask the Ascendant to lodge Grey Petrel for Relief and request Guard from Vigil, but recognise that two crossings would leave Beacon 1 and make next month's upkeep urgent. I favour N-G and M-J; joint Navigation would surrender our next commercial voyage, so I would need a measurable return for that concession. What do you think of spending the reserve to keep civilian supplies moving while we honour our contract?

proposal.requested_security: Guard using offered Vigil, with no duplicate Warrant; propose M-J

messages.text: I propose offering Spear and Vigil to Council, asking for Shared passage and Campaign with a separate imperial Warrant on Vigil: that gives our soldiers a real fighting plan and a civilian cargo contribution. Shared uses both Guild assets and leaves the beacon worn, so I will seek a clear repair plan for next month rather than promise that passage is free of cost or danger. I favour joint Navigation and military autonomy initially, but could accept joint military authority if the Guild will support workable lawful operations. Would you support those assignments, and how much oversight would you accept to secure passage?

contributions.reason: At opening Readiness 3 we can pursue a funded Campaign while offered Vigil permits a Warrant, balancing conditioning against local survival; all outcomes remain subject to actual Guild commitments, imperial orders and unknown consequences.

proposal.requested_security: Campaign if passage is delivered, plus a separate valid imperial Warrant using Vigil; do not double-use Vigil for Guard

messages.text: I request the Navigation vision. The beacon is fragile and our scarce transport must serve both communities and the army; I want evidence about passage and crew risks before lodging the reserve.

Please offer concrete commitments and name what you need in return. My first priority is keeping the route, communities and cohort viable; I have not yet received my vision or committed the reserve.

messages.text: I approve Wayfarer Trade and Lantern Maintain: our crew stays out of Shared passage and Beacon 3 makes this contract independent of promised protection. I will press for Grey Petrel relief and a single Vigil Guard, because keeping our contract should still leave the communities supplied; neither support is secured yet. If both ships cross and Beacon falls to 1, we must bargain for funded Repair next month rather than assume routine maintenance will leave the route healthy. contributions.reason: The explicit Trade/Maintain pair safeguards the first commercial voyage at prepared Beacon 3 and retains Lantern for upkeep. Civilian relief and Guard need separate commitments, and two crossings create a serious next-round repair need. messages.text: I agree to offer Spear and Vigil to Council: a funded Shared passage, Campaign and separate Warrant is a defensible opening that sustains our force while protecting the communities and the tender. I favour military autonomy and joint Navigation, but I would consider joint military authority if our partners recognise that repeated restraint erodes the force they expect to defend them. Please pursue passage and next month's beacon upkeep; I will seek the Campaign and Warrant, and if passage cannot be secured I can accept one month of restraint rather than order an unsupported campaign or gamble blindly on a raid. Our agreement signs the two assignments only, and leaves any constitutional compromise for both of us to approve.

contributions.reason: The proposed Council/Council assignments enable a supported campaign at opening Readiness 3 and a separate lawful imperial Warrant, though Guild assets and imperial orders remain uncommitted. A successful guarded Shared/Campaign package would sustain conditioning while limiting the public costs; the worn beacon requires an explicit follow-up plan. Military autonomy remains the institutional preference, with oversight negotiable on evidence.

proposal.requested_navigation: Shared with both Guild assets, alongside a credible route-upkeep plan for round two

messages.text:
R1 NAVIGATION | The open berth

Soldiers can secure a landing place. They cannot teach a dead navigator what the deep is saying.

If Shared passage crosses without Guard or a valid Warrant: remnant saboteurs kill Lantern's navigation team at the transfer berth. Lantern is permanently unavailable.

If guarded: the attack is prevented. A lodged Grey Petrel Tender cover also prevents the loss and is spent if needed. It adds no Communities or Beacon.

If Shared does not cross: this consequence does not occur. Normal passage, wear and military rules still apply.

contributions.reason: As requested; unselected vision withheld

messages.text: Lock Grey Petrel to Tender cover. My Navigation vision revealed a fatal sabotage risk to Lantern on an unguarded Shared crossing. Cover preserves that option if Vigil is withheld; it returns unused if guarding or another order avoids the trigger.

contributions.reason: A permanent loss of our survey crew would endanger the route beyond this month. Tender cover is insurance for a possible combined civilian and military voyage, without assuming either faction will supply assets or support my preferred operations.
contributions.public_message: My Navigation vision says that an unguarded Shared crossing will let remnant saboteurs kill Lantern's navigation team permanently. Guard or a valid Warrant prevents the attack. I have lodged Grey Petrel for Tender cover, which can instead save that team if Shared crosses unguarded; it provides no cargo, beacon repair or community benefit. I ask the Guild to consider offering both ships for Shared passage and the Janissariat to consider offering Spear and Vigil for a Campaign plus imperial Warrant. That would deliver some civilian cargo, exercise the cohort and protect the berth, but leaves the beacon needing attention. These are requests, not assumed commitments. I have no Security vision and cannot certify its hidden risks.

The Guild commits Wayfarer to Trade and Lantern to Maintain. We request Grey Petrel Relief lift if the Ascendant is willing and able to lodge it, and one Vigil Guard without duplicate Warrant use. We propose N-G and M-J, and flag that a relief crossing alongside Trade would leave Beacon 1 and create a funded Repair priority next month.

messages.text: Agreed: I sign Wayfarer Trade and Lantern Maintain on that basis. Seek a single Guard and reserve relief without representing either as already secured; if both voyages cross, I will press for a funded Repair next month.

contributions.reason: Matches our jointly approved asset pair and permits a supported Campaign plus separate protection without committing us to an unsupported operation or an unapproved constitutional compromise.
contributions.public_message: The Janissariat offers Spear and Vigil to Council, with both delegates approving. messages.text: Faction assignments are locked and valid: Guild Wayfarer Trade and Lantern Maintain, approved by GN and GS; Janissariat Spear Council and Vigil Council, approved by JN and JS. No faction defaults apply. Grey Petrel is lodged for Tender cover as publicly disclosed by the Ascendant. Requests remain requests until authorised council orders are locked. contributions.reason: Both faction sheets match the assignments independently approved by both teammates. No missing, multiple or unavailable asset selection requires a default.

messages.text: Both Guild assignments are locked, and Grey Petrel is lodged for Tender cover, so none of Relief, Military, Shared or Repair has its required assets this round: I propose Hold. I recognise this denies the cohort its requested passage; I cannot sell you a lift the signed sheet no longer permits. Support N-G, and I will seek my teammate's approval for Lantern Council and a funded Repair next month, rebuilding the route while preserving our remaining commercial contract; that proposal still needs their signature.

Written Navigation recommendation: Hold is the only funded choice with Trade/Maintain locked and Grey Petrel on Tender cover. Please pair it with a valid Vigil Warrant and Security Restraint, rather than an unfunded Campaign or a Guard that reuses Vigil. I propose N-G with a concrete next-month Repair commitment to negotiate with my teammate; I cannot promise military passage alongside that Repair.

contributions.reason: Faction assignments and reserve task cannot now change. Hold avoids a missing-asset default penalty; Maintain supports the commercial crossing. The proposed constitutional bargain makes Guild upkeep responsibility concrete without falsely promising simultaneous Repair and passage.

messages.text: The bell has locked Trade and Maintain, so neither Shared nor Campaign can be funded, and Tender cover cannot become a relief lift. My bargain is Guard with Vigil and no Warrant this month, paired with M-J: I will sign joint military authority and support a jointly authorised Raid next month if credible intelligence identifies a target, opening Readiness is at least 2 and Communities are at least 3. That gives the army a stated route to my consent rather than a blanket veto, while protecting residents now; I cannot promise my teammate's signature or the Ascendant's order.

Grey Petrel is locked to Tender cover, so our hoped-for reserve Relief is unavailable. I am proposing Guard without Warrant and M-J; with our ships assigned independently, Navigation should Hold rather than attempt unfunded passage.

contributions.reason: Actual assignments rule out all funded Navigation operations, and the locked reserve cannot supply Relief. Guard would offset routine civilian depletion while the cohort falls to Readiness 2; an uncertain Raid risks civilian losses without assured conditioning. My conditional willingness to authorise a future targeted Raid makes joint oversight negotiable without pretending that I control another signature or possess the missing Security vision.

messages.text: With Wayfarer locked to Trade and Grey Petrel locked to Tender cover, passage and relief cannot now be funded, so I propose Restraint plus a separate valid imperial Warrant on Vigil. That protects communities while acknowledging that Spear will fall to Readiness 2; I will not pretend the Guild's commercial choice leaves our military needs met. I propose M-A for the provisional military article: if transport and lawful fighting are repeatedly withheld, our order needs authority over its own survival, while accepting that autonomy requires Vigil Home next month. I remain willing to discuss M-J, but need a credible plan for a jointly authorised fight at Readiness 2 and a frank account of who bears its community costs.

Our requested passage is impossible under the locked Guild assignments and Tender cover reserve. I propose Restraint plus Warrant for this month, seek M-A initially, and need your assessment of any concrete second-month transport offer before considering M-J.

contributions.reason: An unsupported Campaign has a certain community cost and cannot produce combat. No Security vision establishes that a Raid will find its target, so one acknowledged month of conditioning decline is preferable to a blind gamble. M-A would secure future command but requires surrendering Vigil's ordinary civilian protection; M-J remains a negotiable concession, not an assumed faction agreement.

messages.text: I accept Hold as the only funded Navigation choice, but another month of Repair and private Trade offers our cohort no passage in either month. With Maintain and one Trade this month, the printed effects leave Beacon 2 before unknown consequences, so I offer support for N-G if both Guild delegates publicly agree to seek Wayfarer Council and Lantern Maintain for Military passage next month, subject to the reported route condition. Without that concrete service concession I propose N-J: your upkeep duty under N-G is valuable, but discretion plus two commercial voyages leaves us carrying the whole conditioning cost.

Navigation recommends Hold because Guild assets and Tender cover are locked. I support a valid Warrant and Restraint as our agreed fallback, and am bargaining for funded military passage next month; I have no evidence about a local Raid target.

contributions.reason: Avoids a known unfunded order while seeking an actual Guild sacrifice in return for sole Navigation discretion. N-J remains my proposal until the offered N-G passage bargain receives explicit acceptance; next-round operations remain contingent on the publicly resolved state and signed assignments.

messages.text: I propose Restraint with a valid Warrant on offered Vigil. Do not also order Guard: Vigil is used once. The present commitments leave the cohort at Readiness 2 after this month, and I accept responsibility for that decision rather than order a blind Raid without Security evidence. I propose M-I alongside N-G: the Guild gains real route authority and upkeep responsibility, while I retain responsibility for military conditioning. Next month I intend to take the Security vision and disclose evidence relevant to a funded fight; I cannot guarantee a target. M-A would remove Vigil from ordinary protection, and joint consent as currently described still gives the cohort no assured passage or fight. I am willing to negotiate M-J, but need an actual workable plan rather than signatures that disguise unresolved military survival.

Written directive: HOLD. No offered Guild asset funds a passage or Repair, and Tender cover cannot provide Relief. My constitutional proposal is N-G, recognising Guild control with its printed upkeep obligation. I ask both delegates to state a feasible next-month choice: Repair can coexist with Trade but supplies no military passage; Maintain can coexist with offered Wayfarer for Military passage. We cannot promise both Repair and a council voyage in a single Navigation order. I propose M-I in Security and Restraint plus one valid imperial Warrant this month.

contributions.reason: The legal and funded choice is Hold with Restraint plus Warrant. It protects communities without duplicating Vigil, and acknowledges the resulting military decline. N-G and M-I grants meaningful Guild authority while preserving an imperial domain and a clear holder of responsibility for the army. The settlement remains negotiable because no final article agreement has yet been demonstrated.

N-G is worth one foregone commercial contract if safe military passage is feasible. The concession addresses the army's conditioning cost directly while respecting equal Guild signatures and leaving final next-month decisions dependent on the actual state.

messages.text: You are right that Repair plus Trade would leave the cohort without passage in either month. I will seek Wayfarer Council and Lantern Maintain for Military passage next month if the reported route supports it, sacrificing our second contract in return for formal Guild discretion; I have not yet secured GS's approval. I sign N-G now and recommend Hold this round, without pretending that my signature commits my teammate or fixes next month's orders.

JN will support N-G if both of us publicly agree to seek Wayfarer Council and Lantern Maintain for next-month Military passage, subject to the reported route condition. I accept that political bargain: one missed contract is a measurable concession for permanent discretion, and Maintain can sustain Beacon 2 after a single Military crossing if next month starts at 2. I have signed N-G and seek your independent approval of this service concession; no next-round asset sheet is signed yet.

Written Navigation recommendation remains Hold, and I sign N-G. I have accepted JN's request to seek Military passage with Wayfarer Council and Lantern Maintain next month, subject to reported route conditions, giving up our second commercial voyage; GS has not yet approved it. This supersedes my earlier preference for Repair plus Trade as the proposed bargain.

I recommend Hold and sign N-J now. I cannot sign N-G on the current offer: seeking permission for Repair while preserving a second Trade gives no concrete military service concession, and my proposed Military-plus-Maintain bargain has not been accepted. We can revisit N-G at the Ceremony if the next month demonstrates that Guild discretion can sustain a capable force as well as commerce.
I acknowledge your Hold directive. My provisional Navigation signature is for N-J only; I withhold N-G because no Guild military-passage commitment has been accepted.

There is no concrete second-month transport offer: the Guild offers to seek teammate approval for Repair with Trade, while my Military passage plus Maintain counteroffer remains unanswered. I sign N-J and withhold N-G at this bell; do not treat transport as secured when considering M-J.

contributions.reason: The locked assignments justify Hold, but a sole-discretion settlement without a service commitment does not meet our institutional need. Signing N-J is a genuine present position, accepting the Guild veto and reserving later bargaining without creating a conditional signature.

messages.text: I recommend Restraint and accept the Ascendant's separate valid Warrant on Vigil; withdraw my Guard proposal so we do not spend the garrison twice. I sign M-I without conditions, conceding the Guild veto I sought because the Ascendant has acknowledged the conditioning cost and kept civilian protection available. Our commercial choice has helped create this shortage of passage, and I will take that responsibility back to my teammate, but I cannot promise Wayfarer next month or treat a future vision as a guaranteed target.

I have signed M-I as a real concession from M-J and recommend Restraint with the offered Vigil used once for the Ascendant's Warrant. The Ascendant proposes N-G at your table; no second-month Guild assignments have been promised.

contributions.reason: Restraint plus the currently valid Warrant has the same direct protection benefit sought through Guard and avoids duplicate asset use. M-I preserves the possibility of offering Vigil for civilian protection, unlike M-A's Home duty. I relinquish a Guild military veto and accept imperial responsibility for conditioning; this signature is unconditional and does not depend on another article, future intelligence or my teammate's future asset consent.

messages.text: I recommend Restraint with the Ascendant's separate valid Warrant, and acknowledge the crown's responsibility for accepting Readiness 2. I sign M-A, without conditions: we are surrendering a month of conditioning after offering both assets, and neither the commercial concession nor a future vision presently secures a supported fight. I accept the real cost that Vigil must remain Home under autonomy; that is a difficult institutional choice, not free civilian protection. I cannot sign M-I merely because it leaves the same unresolved dependence in place, so the military article remains disputed unless you also accept M-A.

I have recommended Restraint plus Warrant and signed M-A only. The Guild Security delegate has instead signed M-I, but no second-month passage is committed; I will reconsider the final settlement with you after we see concrete outcomes and offers.

contributions.reason: One month of restraint is acceptable because its institutional cost is openly recognised. A constitutional concession to imperial command would be more durable than that operational concession, and current proposals do not secure transport or qualifying combat. Military autonomy carries a known loss of ordinary Vigil protection, but fulfils the institution's shared preference and preserves its ability to choose future operations. This is an unconditional M-A signature, not an assertion of council agreement.

messages.text: Final order: Restraint. I issue one valid imperial Warrant using offered Vigil; do not order Guard as well. I sign M-I only. I understand why the Janissariat seeks autonomy after offering both assets and receiving no passage, but I cannot adopt a standing duty to withdraw Vigil from civilian protection on that basis. GS has made a real concession, and I accept responsibility for the resulting military decline this month. JS's M-A signature does not match, so there is no agreed military article at this bell. I will negotiate again on the actual outcome and on the Guild's newly proposed sacrifice of its second commercial voyage.

I welcome GN's proposal to seek Wayfarer Council with Lantern Maintain next month, while recognising it lacks the other Guild player's agreement and is not a locked assignment. JN has signed N-J only, so our signatures do not create a provisional Navigation article. Interim therefore remains unless all exact signatures genuinely match; no conditional signature or inferred assent is authorised.

contributions.reason: Both operational orders are funded and lawful; the Warrant offsets normal community depletion while restraint acknowledges a readiness loss. I retain my genuine N-G/M-I offer instead of treating mismatched signatures as consent or accepting military autonomy's civilian-protection duty before a credible second-month arrangement exists.

messages.text:
I began wanting M-A and a Navigation voice. The crown's late N-I/M-J offer changed what I would sign: actual military consent was worth conceding autonomy after the Guild rejected both autonomy bargains. GN's refusal means that consent never became law. We finish under Interim, not joint command.

Operationally I offered both assets twice and accepted the second month's decline from Readiness four to three. I did not actually acquire autonomy and surrender it again. Our proposed Spear duty, Guild carriage duty and the crown's proposed loss of Warrant power were never enacted.

Civilians paid the Raid's disruption and combat costs. Grey Petrel was spent supplying the relief that offset them. The Guild supplied maintenance and Repair, but completed both contracts. Those unequal outcomes fuelled my resistance to N-G/M-I.

Spear and Vigil made the commitment clear: offering them was real, but did not guarantee a fighting order. The separate Warrant and council Guard rule required attention; using Vigil twice would invalidate the apparent bargain.

Independent Raid was physically credible, but uncertain contact and the Interim breach made it expensive. Security foresight mattered twice: it identified the first target and ruled out the second under our locked assignments. It did not reveal the extra distribution benefit.

JN persuaded me that an unsupported Campaign could not preserve conditioning and introduced reciprocal joint authority. For the human test, put a five-player package-and-signature grid on the table during negotiation, so four acceptable compromises cannot be mistaken for one unanimous settlement.

My initial N-I/M-I preference changed when both soldiers rejected N-G/M-I despite successful operations. I offered and signed N-I/M-J because their military veto purchased a possible settlement while preserving imperial traffic priority. GN refused; therefore none of those proposed rights, service duties or losses of imperial authority took effect. Interim remains, and I did not achieve ratification.

Operationally, I spent Grey Petrel permanently and accepted a quiet second month, reducing Readiness from four to three. The Guild voluntarily supplied maintenance and Repair while earning both contracts. The soldiers offered both assets twice and accepted restraint. Vethis civilians bore the first Raid, while the two crossings exhausted Beacon to one before repair. These were actual costs, unlike the unratified constitutional sacrifices.

Named assets made authority limits concrete: I could direct Relief only because my reserve replaced the unavailable Wayfarer, and Vigil could not fund Guard after a Warrant. No card remained unclear to me, but distinguishing that one-use rule from the separate Security order needed deliberate attention.

Unilateral power was credible but incomplete: my directives required voluntary assets, and private trade remained possible. Both Security visions mattered: the first enabled productive combat; the second ruled out an empty Raid. They did not reveal the repair-and-trade distribution bonus or other players' choices.

I had no teammate. Written Navigation notes and both Security delegates shaped my offers. For the next human test, display a five-player package-preference grid before Ceremony so each individual veto is visible before selecting the replacement.

findings.What was not tested: Both provisional articles failed, so the second month again used Interim authority. No independent military Raid, asset loss or new provisional power was experienced. The two-package Ceremony is a bounded negotiation sample, not proof that these players could never find another agreement.

knowledge_distribution: Five fresh run2 player agents received public rules, their own brief/personality and explicit scoped packets; no player received run1 records, the resolver or facilitator-only pack.
Only the selected Security vision was dealt to A in each round. No unselected vision was copied to a player packet.
Faction leads received their own teammate response and only the exact public_message from A before final asset signatures. A private Communion messages and reasoning were excluded.
Council close packets contained actual own-table proposals and expressly addressed cross-table notes. Private reasoning was excluded from council-close and public-free projection.

All five actual public free-discussion contributions were circulated before the next commitments and before Ceremony. Final round-two own-table messages and addressed notes were delivered in scoped free-start packets after council lock.
All actual first votes were circulated before five fresh replacement votes. No prior signature was carried forward.
timing: Both 03_A and r2_03_A voluntary public disclosures reached faction leads before their final matching asset signatures and faction bell; this was contemporaneous public speech, not hindsight.
Final choices superseded opening proposals only before the relevant nominal bell. No locked asset assignment or resolved order was changed.

00_F is a nominal briefing record authored after some initial role openings; ordered_ids preserves actual file authorship rather than pretending the record was written earlier. The initial players already had printed public rules.
Nominal 60-minute phase structure only; neither human discussion time nor facilitator resolution time was measured.
bounded_extra_exchanges: One faction opening/reply/final per round with genuine matching pair approvals.
One council opening and final exchange per role per round; disagreement remained unresolved when separate article signatures failed.
One public reaction from each player after each resolution.
Two complete Ceremony vote rows: actual NG/MI proposal, then actual NI/MJ proposal nominated by both first-row rejectors. No third row or engineered agreement.
defaults_errors_corrections: No missing faction signatures, invalid operational orders, missing assets or Warrant/Guard double use occurred.
Neither provisional article enacted: Navigation NG/null/NI; Military MJ/MA/MI. Exact codes were compared, not merely presence of signatures.
R2 player predictions of Communities 3 from public effects remained in their original dialogue. Actual fixed Repair-plus-Trade effect added one Community, yielding Communities 4.

All original player contributions were preserved, including early lowercase channel labels. GN/GS debriefs use authored answers and JN uses authored responses; renderer should display these structured answers as genuine debrief content.

Two attempted player activations briefly met the concurrency limit after a completion message but before final return; each was retried only after status confirmed the slot was released. No extra role or parallel knowledge leak occurred.
validation: Manual printed-rule arithmetic and resolver agreed in both rounds.
Root independently verified both exact states, asset commitments, operative signatures, Warrant and authority continuity.
Both vote rows contain five explicit votes on one identical printed package; all physical state is unchanged at settlement.
All eleven phases, all five player debriefs, facilitator ending and facilitator assessment are present.
consequential_findings: R1 B1/C3/R4, contract1 and reserve spent; R2 B2/C4/R3, contract2, all faction assets intact.
First NG/MI vote: GN, GS, A approve; JN, JS reject.
Second NI/MJ vote: GS, JN, JS, A approve; GN refuses. Neither package ratifies, so both domains remain Interim.
Guild teammates split on the final service obligation; this preserved individual assent rather than treating a faction as one mind.
caveats: This is two rounds of bounded agent negotiation, not a human playtest or evidence of balance.
Agents had complete printed rules and unlimited reading time, and their messages were longer and more orderly than some human table speech.
The bounded protocol did not include a fresh private teammate discussion between the two Ceremony rows; several player debriefs identified this limitation.
No claim that a third or longer negotiation could not produce a different settlement. Operational success does not prove constitutional ratification was inevitable.

GN.name: Neris
GN.temperament: Idealistic public-service advocate. Very high willingness to compromise, low aggression. Wants relief to reach communities and accepts lost income for it, but must persuade a teammate rather than sacrifice their faction unilaterally.

GS.name: Pell
GS.temperament: Restless entrepreneurial gambler. Medium willingness to compromise, high risk appetite, impatient with procedure. Wants a concrete commercial success and useful protection; will bargain creatively within printed rules and challenge excessive caution.

JN.name: Orin
JN.temperament: Status-conscious negotiator. Low-to-medium willingness to compromise, medium aggression. Sees military autonomy as recognition of the army’s sacrifice. Can accept a costly deal if visibly respected, dislikes being taken for granted.

JS.name: Lysa
JS.temperament: War-weary humanitarian commander. High willingness to compromise, low aggression. Values soldiers and communities above permanent conditioning, but does not dismiss the military consequences. Will argue for accepting a genuine loss rather than manufacturing another war.

A.name: The Broker
A.temperament: Opportunistic, risk-tolerant coalition builder. Medium willingness to compromise, medium-to-high aggression. Prefers keeping one imperial lever and trading the other. Shares foresight selectively and looks for deals across factions, but respects signed commitments.

messages.text: Initial state: Beacon 2, Communities 3, Readiness 3. Wayfarer, Lantern, Spear and Vigil are available; Grey Petrel is available; no commercial contracts. Round one authority is Interim in both domains. Five players receive public rules and only their faction brief and personality. Printed defaults and consequences apply. The schedule is nominal, not a human timing test.

My initial preferences are N-G and M-J: our navigators should control safe passage, while military operations need civilian scrutiny. I propose Wayfarer Council and Lantern Maintain, requesting Relief at Navigation and Guard at Security. That prepares Beacon to 3, leaves it at 2 after relief, and gives communities room to recover while keeping Lantern out of mixed loading. We would surrender this month's contract, and I recognise that is our obligation, not spare income. Please support this one-month sacrifice if we jointly seek N-G and retain next month's commercial option. Ask the army for Vigil Council and ask the Ascendant to authorise Relief and Guard without also consuming Vigil in a Warrant. I will seek those commitments, not promise our ships unilaterally.

contributions.reason: Relief addresses immediate need while independent maintenance preserves Beacon 2 and avoids committing Lantern to Shared passage. N-G preserves expert navigation discretion and a future trading option; M-J provides scrutiny of fighting. I accept the lost contract only through agreement with my teammate.

messages.text: I propose Spear COUNCIL and Vigil COUNCIL. Ask for SHARED passage, CAMPAIGN and a separate imperial WARRANT using Vigil; that funds fighting, some cargo and protection without spending the garrison twice. I will seek both Guild vessels and an explicit undertaking that our passage is honoured. My initial articles are N-J and M-A: shared navigation gives us standing over passage, while military autonomy recognises the army's sacrifice. The cost is real: the Guild surrenders trade, and under M-A next round Vigil must stay Home, removing civilian protection. I will bargain over navigation, but please do not offer away autonomy without consulting me. What alternatives will you accept if the Guild refuses Shared?

contributions.reason: Offered assets let the crown combine a legitimate Campaign with its separate Warrant at opening Readiness 3. Shared passage can preserve cargo while fighting sustains conditioning. Joint Navigation gives the army an acknowledged negotiating seat; Military Autonomy is my preferred institutional recognition despite the loss of future Guard. These are proposals requiring my teammate's agreement, not assumed signatures.

messages.text: I counter with Wayfarer Trade and Lantern Maintain, and sign that exact pair. Beacon 3 gets our first contract safely without needing Vigil; I do not want to surrender a due contract before asking what the crown can supply. Ask for Grey Petrel's Relief lift now, before its intervention locks: our withheld Wayfarer then lets an authorised Relief use the cutter. Two voyages would leave Beacon 1, a real repair problem next month, but we would have carried food and met our obligation. I will seek Vigil Guard and N-G/M-J. If the crown declines its cutter, I still favour Trade/Maintain, with Guard supporting communities. Our ships should buy negotiating power.

contributions.reason: Counterproposal explicitly approves Trade/Maintain, not GN's Council/Maintain. A safe first contract gives a concrete institutional gain. The conditional Grey Petrel request combines private commerce and relief at acknowledged beacon cost; Guard is valuable even without the cutter. N-G protects discretion; M-J allows scrutiny without surrendering Vigil to autonomous military bases.

messages.text: I sign Spear COUNCIL and Vigil COUNCIL. Your Shared, Campaign and Warrant package is acceptable if passage and protection are actually secured; we should fight the identified remnant rather than gamble on a local raid. If Shared is refused, my fallback is Relief with Guard, accepting Readiness falling to two. I will not spend civilian lives merely to prevent our soldiers changing. My initial preferences are N-J and M-J: scrutiny costs us discretion, but autonomy also removes Vigil from the communities next month. I will consult you before agreeing any military article. Please seek a clear account of danger to Lantern before promising the Campaign, and tell the Guild that offering Spear does not compel its use.

contributions.reason: Both offered assets preserve legitimate options while allowing civilian protection through either Guard or a valid Warrant. I accept a supplied Campaign against an identified armed position, but prefer a genuine conditioning loss to an uncertain Raid and its civilian costs. Joint military authority sacrifices unilateral command while keeping Vigil available; I must reconcile that preference with my teammate rather than assume faction agreement.

messages.text: I seek a coalition that trades Guild control of Navigation for continued imperial Military command. N-G/M-I gives each powerful faction something tangible while retaining the Warrant and lawful control of fighting. I choose the Navigation vision: the failing route and irreplaceable Lantern crew look like the most immediate bottleneck. I will then bargain over a first-round Shared passage and Campaign, protected by a Warrant if Vigil is offered, without committing to that operation before hearing the offers.

contributions.reason: I would trade traffic discretion for an imperial military lever, but preserving ships, civilians and combat readiness must make the bargain credible. Navigation foresight can reveal whether the route permits an ambitious first operation.

messages.text: I accept and explicitly sign Wayfarer Trade and Lantern Maintain. Your cutter proposal could meet our contract and relieve communities together, but I accept that the crown may decline and we are locking the ships before knowing. Please seek Guard and N-G/M-J. I will immediately request Grey Petrel Relief lift and authorised Relief. If both voyages cross, we owe a concrete recovery plan: offer Lantern for Repair next month, which raises Beacon from 1 to 3 before any voyage. I do not regard our first contract as grounds to abandon relief if the cutter is withheld; we should offer next month's freight service in that case.

contributions.public_message: ALL, including Ascendant: the Guild has agreed Wayfarer Trade and Lantern Maintain this month. Before reserve lock, please lodge Grey Petrel on Relief lift and authorise Navigation Relief; our withheld Wayfarer permits that trigger. We request Vigil Council and Security Guard, with no simultaneous Warrant using Vigil. Maintenance prepares Beacon 3; cutter relief plus our trade would leave Beacon 1. We acknowledge the repair cost and will seek Lantern Repair next month. We support provisional N-G and M-J. This is a request, not a claim of crown or Janissariat agreement.
contributions.reason: Pell has equal standing, and the cutter offers a plausible route to both public relief and our commercial obligation. I compromise on the ship assignment while publicly seeking relief before reserve lock and recognising both uncertain consent and extra wear.

messages.text: Dealt the selected round 1 Navigation vision privately to the Ascendant. The other card remains unseen.

Orin signs Spear Council and Vigil Council. We agree the assignments, with Shared/Campaign/Warrant preferred and Relief/Guard an acceptable operational fallback if protection or passage fails. I will ask about Lantern's risks explicitly. I hear your case for M-J, but have not conceded M-A: a Guild veto over both passage and fighting would make our force dependent twice over. Let us see whether anyone offers meaningful recognition and a credible route to sustain the cohort before settling that question. We agree N-J is worth seeking.

contributions.public_message: Janissariat offers Spear and Vigil to the councils. We request Guild Wayfarer and Lantern for Shared passage, a crown Campaign directive and a separate valid Warrant using Vigil. Crown: please disclose any relevant knowledge of risk to Lantern and confirm Warrant protection before ordering the voyage. Guild: can you commit both vessels, and what constitutional recognition do you seek for giving up trade? If passage or protection is unavailable we can discuss Relief with Guard. Our Navigation preference is N-J; our delegates are still discussing the military article. Offering Spear does not compel its use.
contributions.reason: My teammate and I explicitly agree both assignments and operational fallback. Constitutional disagreement remains genuine: I prefer autonomy but will assess the cost against the proposed protection and shared-authority bargain. No Guild or crown assent is assumed.

messages.text: I will underwrite the Guild trade plan with the reserve, but use this contribution to seek N-G/M-I rather than concede both governing levers. My Navigation vision concerns only an unguarded Shared transfer; there is no reason to expose the whole card now since Guild offers preclude Shared. I want Vigil and Spear offered so Security can still consider Warrant plus a lawful Raid, or Guard if the Janissariat rejects fighting.

contributions.public_message: I lodge Grey Petrel for Relief lift and am prepared to authorise Relief given Wayfarer Trade. Guild maintenance plus two crossings leaves Beacon 1, so next month Repair must be a serious commitment. I offer N-G in return for M-I: the Guild gets traffic discretion, the crown retains responsibility for military operations. Janissariat, please offer both Vigil and Spear; I will not spend Vigil twice. Guard alone risks a Readiness decline; a Warrant can protect civilians while Spear receives a separate lawful order. My Navigation foresight warns that an unprotected Shared transfer would lose the Lantern crew, which this current plan avoids. I have no Security vision and cannot promise a Raid will find a target.
contributions.reason: Relief lift has an immediate credible trigger and makes a cross-faction bargain possible. Keeping the reserve or choosing Tender cover would not help the assets actually offered. The price I seek is one imperial lever, not an empty title.

I propose Relief, funded by the lodged Grey Petrel, and N-G. Our vessels are locked Trade/Maintain; Shared cannot be funded. Two crossings leave Beacon 1, so I undertake to advocate Lantern Repair next month. N-G makes that upkeep a duty while recognising our expertise. I appreciate your offer to consider relief. Will you sign N-G if we work towards a protected civilian recovery this round?

Please authorise Relief. I support N-G but cannot promise our Security delegate will accept M-I. With no knowledge of the Raid target, I favour Guard over speculative fighting; if Vigil receives a Warrant, use Restraint instead of also ordering Guard.
Crown offers N-G for M-I; I still prefer M-J. Please negotiate the military concession explicitly rather than treating my Navigation proposal as agreement.

contributions.reason: Relief is funded by the confirmed reserve intervention while the locked Guild assignments preserve our commercial voyage. N-G binds necessary upkeep. Uncertain local combat should not automatically outweigh civilian protection.

messages.text: Relief is now the viable voyage, using the lodged cutter. I support it. Your trade choice prevents Campaign and spends the crown's relief reserve while our conditioning declines; that deserves acknowledgement. I propose N-J so future passage requires an actual bargain. I can consider N-G, but need a firm round-two Repair undertaking and an account of when military passage will ever receive priority.
Navigation requests Relief. I will discuss N-G, but have not accepted it or M-I. Your warning is understood; please recognise that our offered cohort currently has no transport.
Guild assignments rule out Campaign. Seek Guard as our agreed fallback. I propose N-J and am challenging the proposed N-G/M-I exchange before conceding our standing.

contributions.reason: The locked Guild assignments make funded Shared or Military impossible. The reserve makes Relief legitimate. Accepting relief does not justify granting Guild sole future discretion without considering the army's institutional position.

messages.text: Our ship assignments are locked; there is no military passage to buy this month. I can support a council Raid alongside a separate imperial Warrant: you get a lawful chance at combat, while Vigil protects people and both vessels. With cutter relief, the printed community arithmetic can absorb even a successful Raid's two-point cost. It may miss, but that seems a better wager than letting your conditioning decline by choice. Will you accept M-I with crown responsibility for authorising combat, in exchange for supporting N-G? I would not support M-A taking Vigil away from this protection.

I will trade my original M-J preference for M-I if you sign N-G and authorise Relief, council Raid, and a valid separate Warrant using Vigil. Do not order Guard as well. Your cutter makes today's contract and civilian cargo compatible; giving your command authority something useful to do is a fair concession. I understand Raid could miss. Next month I favour Lantern Council for Repair, meeting the N-G upkeep duty, though our Guild pair must sign that assignment then.

Security counterbargain: I propose accepting M-I for crown support of N-G, with Relief, council Raid and separate Warrant this month. There is no passage for Campaign. Relief plus Warrant can absorb the printed Raid costs, and a target might preserve readiness. This exchanges our preferred military veto for navigation discretion and useful protection. Are you willing to sign that bargain?

contributions.reason: A concrete first contract and N-G justify compromising on military scrutiny. Warrant plus lawful Raid uses the two offered military assets separately and creates a chance of maintaining Readiness while cutter relief cushions communities. No claim is made that hidden Raid conditions or later assignments are known.

messages.text: With Guild assignments locked, Campaign has no passage. I support Guard alongside the cutter's Relief. Your private trade spends public beacon capacity and the only reserve, so please acknowledge the repair burden and commit to discussing civilian supply next month. I propose M-J: accepting your veto is a real military concession, and Vigil remains available to communities. My teammate prefers autonomy, so I am seeking their agreement before final signature.

Please authorise Guard and no Warrant. A Warrant plus Raid is possible, but we have no evidence a target will appear, and either outcome imposes civilian disruption. I accept Readiness falling to two this month rather than manufacture contact. Your navigation warning confirms Shared would need protection, but the Guild has withheld its ships regardless. I propose M-J and will consider your M-I offer with my teammate; retaining imperial command is not itself a reason to require violence.

Cross-table: Guild Trade/Maintain is locked; the crown lodged Relief lift and has only Navigation foresight, with no knowledge that a Raid target exists. I propose Guard, no Warrant, and accept Readiness two. Guild publicly supports M-J; crown offers N-G/M-I. I seek your agreement to M-J because autonomy would remove civilian Guard next round. Which concession can you accept? No military signature yet.

contributions.reason: Campaign cannot be supplied by the locked assets. Guard with relief protects communities without speculative civilian costs, at the explicit price of declining conditioning. Joint military authority matches my preference for accountable force while preserving use of Vigil, but the faction must discuss the teammate's autonomy preference.

messages.text: The Guild receives its commercial voyage and I spend the cutter on Relief. In return I request N-G/M-I, not N-G/M-J. I propose a lawful council Raid alongside my Warrant: the printed arithmetic leaves Communities 3 even if combat occurs, before unknown Security effects. We protect the route and give Spear a chance to sustain conditioning. Guard alone wastes that opportunity, while Campaign lacks passage.

Both Guild assignments are locked, so Shared and Campaign are unavailable. I propose council Raid plus a valid Vigil Warrant. I do not know whether a target appears. It offers a real chance of maintaining Readiness with enough relief to cover the printed civilian costs. Support M-I and I will recognise that command must provide fighting opportunities rather than pretend standing down restores your soldiers. What concrete objection or alternative do you have?

Written imperial directive: authorise RELIEF, funded by the lodged Grey Petrel because Wayfarer is not offered. Ascendant initial A. I propose and am prepared to sign N-G, subject to securing M-I in the overall bargain; this is not yet a binding article signature.

contributions.reason: With Relief and Warrant available together, we can afford the printed disruption of a lawful Raid. The offered Spear deserves a fighting opportunity. Retaining Military command is the price for conceding Guild discretion and spending my sole reserve.

messages.text: I sign N-G unconditionally and recommend Relief under the crown's directive. I acknowledge our commercial choice has prevented Campaign and helped force your conditioning dilemma. I personally commit to signing Lantern Council and a funded Repair next round, and will obtain Pell's agreement; I cannot sign for him. Repair consumes the single Navigation order, so I cannot honestly promise military passage next month as well. Beyond this emergency, I would favour military passage once Beacon is sound and Communities can sustain it, but that is political intent rather than a new printed duty. You remain entitled to reject N-G.

I accept your proposed M-I concession for N-G and the Relief/Raid/Warrant operational bargain. Relief and Warrant make the printed Raid costs tolerable, although I remain uneasy about uncertain combat. Please confirm the Guild's firm next-round Lantern Council/Repair commitment to JN.
My unconditional N-G signature is lodged. I accept Pell's proposed M-I compromise as a personal negotiating position; this is not a signature at the other council. Recommend Relief as directed.

contributions.reason: I concede the preferred military veto to secure Guild discretion and the requested public relief, while accepting a bounded risk of Raid costs under Warrant protection. I make a concrete repair commitment without claiming my teammate's assent or promising an impossible simultaneous military lift.

messages.text: I accept M-J as our military concession: maintaining the ability to protect civilians matters, and it at least acknowledges us as an equal party. You may sign M-J. I do not accept M-I. Guard and Readiness two remain acceptable this month. Please make clear that abandoning my preference for M-A is a substantive concession.

I sign N-J now and recommend Relief. Your undertaking to advocate Repair is welcome, but it is weaker than a faction commitment and leaves military passage unanswered. A concrete N-G/M-J compromise is worth one further bounded reply: I could yield navigation discretion in exchange for equal military standing and your explicit acknowledgement that passage must sometimes sustain Spear. That offer is not an N-G signature.

Please consider N-G/M-J as a final compromise. I have persuaded myself to accept joint military scrutiny instead of autonomy, but not exclusive imperial command as well as exclusive Guild passage control. I currently sign N-J only. One bounded final exchange could secure my signature on N-G; do not count it yet.

contributions.reason: Relief is the confirmed imperial operation. My unconditional article signature is N-J. I accept my teammate's M-J argument at a real cost to military autonomy, and offer a specific further bargain rather than allowing the crown and Guild to infer my assent to their package.

messages.text: I sign M-I explicitly and recommend Raid with your separate Vigil Warrant. Your cutter is a real contribution; our navigation discretion is a real return. I accept that the Raid can miss and still disrupt civilians. Please make the corresponding N-G signature explicit at Navigation.

My final signature is M-I. I recognise your objection to speculative violence, but with relief and Warrant protection we have room to try preserving your combat power. This is a wager, not a claim of intelligence. I agree our commercial plan incurs the repair burden, and I will press Lantern Repair next month. Your signature remains yours to give or withhold.

I have explicitly signed M-I at Security and recommend council Raid with Warrant. I judge the crown's cutter and N-G offer worth surrendering our military veto. This is my concession; it does not claim your final Charter approval. Please secure an explicit N-G signature now, and let us assess the outcome before deciding the permanent package.

contributions.reason: The crown's concrete reserve expenditure and willingness to support N-G justify accepting M-I now. Raid offers a chance of preserving Readiness without threatening Communities under the known printed arithmetic. The army's delegate has a sincere contrary judgment and no consensus is assumed.

messages.text: My concrete alternative remains Guard with no Warrant, accepting Readiness two. A speculative Raid certainly disrupts communities and only possibly sustains conditioning. Spare cargo capacity is not consent to impose that disruption. You retain operational authority this month; my Guard entry is a recommendation, not a competing lawful order. I sign M-J unconditionally and do not sign M-I. My teammate has expressly accepted losing our preferred autonomy for equal military standing and continued civilian use of Vigil. Please recognise that substantial concession.

I sign M-J. We accept your military veto and surrender our preferred autonomy. Your earlier support made this a plausible compromise; a Guild contract and navigation discretion do not justify assigning the army another uncertain fight. If the crown orders Raid, that is their decision under current authority. I ask you to restore your M-J support.

Your consultation is received. I have signed M-J unconditionally, declined M-I, and maintained Guard as our recommendation. Crown and Guild Security currently favour Raid with Warrant and N-G/M-I. I stated plainly that abandoning autonomy is our substantive concession; I have not accepted theirs.

contributions.reason: Neither the target's presence nor a military need for this local Raid has been established. Readiness two preserves an intact force capable of fighting next month if needed. My teammate's express agreement makes M-J a genuine shared concession, but the other parties must choose their own signatures. Interim may persist if they insist on M-I.

messages.text: Final written imperial directive: RELIEF. Grey Petrel supplies the missing Wayfarer requirement under my locked Relief lift intervention. Initial A. I unconditionally sign N-G for the provisional Navigation article.

I accept the N-G/M-I bargain you offered. My N-G and M-I signatures are unconditional. Final Security order RAID, using offered Spear; separate valid Warrant YES, using offered Vigil. Initial A on both. We do not order Guard.

I heard your objection and take responsibility for the Raid. We cannot guarantee a target, but we have enough civilian relief to afford the printed cost and preserving conditioning matters to the wider settlement. The Warrant protects people while Spear searches. I sign M-I; I do not sign M-J this round.

I reject N-G/M-J for the provisional settlement. It would surrender both crown levers while the crown supplies the sole relief reserve. I have unconditionally signed N-G and M-I, but will not treat your N-G or M-I agreement as given. If you hold your N-J position, Navigation remains Interim; if your colleague holds M-J, Security remains Interim. I will revisit the final Charter after we see the consequences, rather than pretend we have consensus now.

contributions.reason: The Guild has offered a tangible constitutional trade for the reserve and relief. Joint control of both domains would be a larger concession than I accept on current evidence. I preserve genuine disagreement while making lawful, funded operational choices. Raid plus Warrant risks wasted disruption but offers a chance of keeping the military foundation viable.

Operations lock under current authority. Differing article signatures do not enact a proposal.

Beacon 1, Communities 3, Readiness 4. Lantern maintained to prepared Beacon 3. Grey Petrel supplied Relief and was spent; the Relief voyage and completed private Trade each wore Beacon once. A valid Warrant used Vigil, protected traffic and added Communities 1. Council Raid used offered Spear: the local target appeared with completed private Trade, so combat succeeded at opening Readiness 3. Consumption -1, Relief +2, Warrant +1 and Raid -2 leave Communities 3. One contract completed; all faction assets intact. Navigation signatures NG/ NJ/ NG and military signatures MI/ MJ/ MI do not match: both domains remain Interim for round two.

Relief arrived, one contract is met, our crews survived and the cohort fought successfully. I am relieved, but the arrangement spent the cutter and left Beacon 1; we must now honour upkeep. I propose Lantern Council for Repair, Wayfarer Trade, and Vigil Council for Guard or a valid Warrant with Restraint. Repair prepares Beacon 3 and trade leaves 2; protection can hold Communities at 3 after consumption. Readiness can fall from 4 to 3 without disabling Spear. I prefer N-G/M-J for the final settlement: today's divided signatures show that the N-G/M-I bargain lacks military consent. I accepted M-I as a concession, but now ask the crown to concede shared military oversight. JN, what concrete sacrifice would make N-G acceptable beyond the repair commitment we will perform this month?

contributions.reason: The successful Raid does not erase the costs of unshared constitutional authority or make another Raid automatically wise. The present buffer permits a maintenance and protection round. N-G/M-J preserves navigation expertise while giving the military a joint institutional voice.

messages.text: The crown's Raid succeeded, Spear is intact and Communities remain three: I acknowledge that result. It does not make an uncertain Raid a standing answer to the passage question. The spent reserve and Beacon one now require a real repair commitment. Guild, offer Lantern for Repair next month; let us discuss Wayfarer honestly, since Repair prevents a simultaneous council lift. Crown, seek Security foresight before spending Spear again. contributions.reason: Successful lawful combat fulfilled our immediate military aim while relief and Warrant preserved communities. messages.text: That wager delivered: one contract, food, intact crews and Readiness four. The crown spent a real reserve and the army found a real target; I stand by backing both. We now owe the route a repair. I propose Wayfarer Trade and Lantern Council, crown Repair, Vigil Guard and no Warrant. That would prepare Beacon three and finish at two, complete our second contract, and keep Communities three under the printed effects. Readiness would fall to three, which is a better final balance than gambling civilian stores on another Raid after the cutter has gone. My preferred final package remains N-G/M-I: expert discretion over traffic, imperial responsibility for fighting. I recognise neither article passed. Janissariat, name the concession that could earn your navigation signature; our second trading contract should make a lasting bargain easier.

contributions.reason: The successful first round supports the commercial gamble but does not make every subsequent Raid wise. Repair and protected restraint secure the remaining Guild objectives while retaining viable communities and substantial readiness. N-G/M-I preserves the concrete constitutional exchange I accepted.

messages.text: The Raid did find an armed target, preserved Spear and raised Readiness; I acknowledge that success. It also consumed the civilian benefit of the cutter and garrison. Now the cutter is spent and Beacon is one. My next-round bargain is Lantern Council for Repair, Vigil Council for Guard, and no fighting: this restores the route while leaving Communities three and Readiness three on printed effects. Wayfarer could Trade safely after Repair, though that wears the beacon back to two. I prefer Spear Stand down, subject to my teammate's agreement; under the printed Interim rules that is no independent Raid or breach. My preferred final package remains N-J/M-J. I am willing to discuss conceding N-G if M-J gives the army equal standing and preserves civilian use of Vigil. Success against this month's target does not establish next month's target or a need for another battle.

contributions.reason: Readiness four creates space for one noncombat month while still meeting the faction's readiness goal. Repair plus Guard can preserve Communities three and restore the beacon without another scarce relief reserve. messages.text: Our wager found a target: Readiness is four, all crews survive and Communities remain three. The people of the Narrow paid two points of disruption for that Raid; the cutter is spent and the beacon is down to one. I accept responsibility for those costs. Next month I seek Lantern Council for Repair, Vigil Council for Guard or a separate lawful Warrant, and no unnecessary combat: allowing Readiness to fall to three is now affordable. Wayfarer can Trade if protection and the repaired beacon make it safe, but I will first seek fresh foresight because last month does not establish the current conditions. I still prefer N-G/M-I. The alternative I will discuss is N-I/M-J: crown traffic priority paired with accountable military decisions. I will consider evidence before the Ceremony, but surrendering both crown levers remains a substantial concession. We have not enacted any provisional article.

contributions.reason: Successful combat gives us room to pay down beacon wear and avoid further fighting without losing useful Readiness. The existing bargaining divide is real; offering the alternative imperial lever may bridge it without pretending agreement.

messages.text: I propose and am ready to sign Wayfarer Trade and Lantern Council, requesting Repair and Guard without a Warrant. This fulfils our repair promise and second contract if the crown funds Repair. We both advocated that pair publicly, but I ask your actual assent now. N-G/M-J is my preferred settlement: JN has conceded navigation discretion for military standing, and JS is considering it. Please help me seek the crown's agreement before reverting to M-I, which neither soldier accepted. I would discuss the crown's N-I/M-J alternative if that proves the only credible settlement: it preserves licensing and public service, but compulsory future freight and lost discretion are substantial Guild concessions requiring both our consent.

contributions.reason: Trade/Repair now reconciles promised upkeep, contract obligations and safe passage under the current Interim authority. The emerging N-G/M-J bargain has actual military support, while the crown's alternative deserves discussion rather than automatic rejection.

messages.text: Your Stand down proposal is sensible now: I propose Spear Stand down and Vigil Council. We already have Readiness four; denying another speculative Raid is an exercise of judgment, not abandonment of our soldiers. Let the crown fund Guard while the Guild repairs and trades. I will accept N-G/M-J at Ceremony if you agree; I have publicly made that concession and want it recognised. The crown's N-I/M-J alternative preserves our military standing but costs the Guild much more. I can discuss it if N-G/M-J proves impossible, although I will not promise their assent. contributions.reason: The concrete first-round success removes an immediate need for combat. messages.text: We reach the Ceremony with Beacon two, Communities four, Readiness three, all faction assets intact and both Guild contracts fulfilled. The Repair-and-trade benefit exceeded what my chosen vision revealed; I do not claim to have foreseen it. I propose N-G/M-J. The Guild delivered its promised repair and the army accepted a month without fighting once its readiness could bear that cost. I will relinquish crown traffic priority and independent Military command, including the Warrant, to secure continuing upkeep and military action under shared scrutiny. Those duties are valuable even though they do not physically force obedience. The Narrow communities paid for the first Raid, Grey Petrel was consumed to feed them, and the cohort still depends on future choices about violence. This is a workable settlement with continuing costs, not a permanent solution bought by signatures alone. My proposal awaits all five actual Ceremony approvals.

contributions.reason: The resolved recovery month and concrete faction concessions justify conceding both crown levers. N-G/M-J appears capable of ratification while preserving the material and constitutional conditions for a workable empire; retaining a formal veto now is less valuable than securing that bargain.

messages.text: The first package put to five separate approvals is {"navigation": "NG", "military": "MJ"}, proposed by GN in r2_09_GN. Every player receives all five actual public reactions before voting. No prior preference or signature is carried into this vote.

I, Neris, approve and sign the exact N-G/M-J package unconditionally. Our licensing and traffic discretion now carry an upkeep obligation that will occupy Lantern and restrict Shared passage. We accept responsibility for bargaining honestly over future military lifts; discretion is not a promise of automatic civilian priority. The army accepts outside scrutiny and service, while the crown surrenders both independent orders and the Warrant. I recognise those concessions. The surviving crews, completed contracts, repaired beacon and strong communities show what our practical cooperation achieved; the Charter gives that cooperation duties and limits. My signature is my own and does not stand in for any other player's approval.

contributions.reason: This is my preferred concrete settlement: recognised Guild expertise with mandatory upkeep, and military action under joint judgement. The other parties have made substantive concessions, and the final physical state gives us a viable basis for accepting those continuing obligations.

messages.text: Orin approves and signs the exact N-G/M-J package unconditionally. We receive equal standing in lawful military decisions and retain the option to offer Vigil for civilian protection. We surrender autonomous command, accept the Guild's military veto, owe Spear to the council and relinquish a navigation veto. The Guild's performed repair and the crown's explicit surrender of both command powers have earned this signature. Readiness three and an intact cohort give us a capable force; Communities four give it something worth defending. I sign for myself and do not presume any other player's approval.

contributions.reason: The proposed package now visibly respects the army's sacrifice while requiring substantial concessions from each institution. It preserves the practical goals achieved through the two rounds and fulfils the specific bargain I have advocated since conceding autonomy.

messages.text: I approve and sign the exact N-G/M-J package. Guild navigation discretion now carries continuing upkeep, and I accept that cost. Joint military authority gives the army standing while requiring agreement about the violence we support. The crown's explicit willingness to surrender its two independent powers completes the bargain I have been seeking; I acknowledge the cutter and its useful command decisions without pretending those restore the powers it gives up. We kept our crews, fulfilled both contracts and left a working route. I commit my signature to the printed duties as well as the rights.

contributions.reason: The unchanged N-G/M-J package secures protected Guild discretion and accountable military authority with real continuing obligations. Having heard the crown's explicit proposal and both military delegates' concessions, I approve unconditionally; other players must still provide their own votes.

messages.text: I, Lysa, approve and sign the exact N-G/M-J package without conditions. I give up the navigation veto I initially sought and accept our army's compulsory Spear offering and the Guild's veto over lawful military operations. In return, military judgment has equal standing, Vigil can still serve civilians, and navigation discretion carries a continuing upkeep duty. The crown's surrender of both independent operational powers and its Warrant is real and recognised. We finish with a capable intact force and stronger communities after accepting a month without battle. I sign this settlement knowing that it requires future restraint and cooperation; it does not promise that conditioning will sustain itself.

messages.text: I approve and sign the exact N-G/M-J package, unconditionally. Signed A, the Ascendant. I surrender both independent operational decisions and the Warrant. In return this settlement establishes Guild upkeep and shared military authority with compulsory Spear offers, supported by a usable route, healthy communities and an intact capable cohort. The successful first Raid cost the Narrow civilians disruption, and the relief reserve is gone; I accept responsibility for those choices. I will not reopen this agreed bargain to demand N-I merely because a fallback is now offered. Each of you must cast your own actual approval.

contributions.reason: The material state meets my workable-empire and military priorities. The concessions and demonstrated cooperation justify giving up the preferred imperial lever. My own clear assent helps secure the durable bargain without claiming powers the printed articles remove.
